deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 51-53): Grothendieck is axiomatising stratifications in a purely topological setting. This feeds his 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) project, which reappears in the Esquisse (1984). A partition (F_i) of a space X into nonempty 'leaves' is called admissible (defined on the next page) if four conditions hold: it is a partition; it is locally finite; each closure F̄_i is a union of leaves (the frontier condition); and each F_i is open in its closure, i.e. locally closed. The closed leaves are ordered by inclusion of closures.

This page has two parts.

(1) It lists extra conditions one may impose on an admissible partition to make it a genuine 'tame stratification':
- (a) connected leaves;
- (b) non-singular leaves, meaning manifolds of a given type, e.g. L.P.M. (probably 'linéaire par morceaux', PL) or S.A.P.M. (probably 'semi-analytique/semi-algébrique par morceaux');
- (c) equisingularity along the strata (Whitney/Thom-Mather type conditions).

NB: admissibility, (b) and (c) are stable under restriction to an open set U. Connectedness (a) is not, since U∩F_i can be disconnected. So Grothendieck proposes a stable replacement (C). Each F_i is connected, and for every open U, the family of connected components of the U∩F_i is again an admissible partition of U. Concretely:
- for each i, the components of U∩F_i form a locally finite family;
- for components F_{iα} of U∩F_i and F_{jβ} of U∩F_j, F_{jβ}∩F̄_{iα}≠∅ implies F_{jβ}⊂F̄_{iα};
- equivalently, F̄_{iα}∩F_j∩U is open (and, implicitly, closed) in F_j∩U.
This is the 'local frontier condition': near each point of a stratum S, the closure of a component of an adjacent stratum T meets S in an open subset. The margin of p.51 says it is a local condition on germs. It is exactly the topological shadow of local conic structure / local topological triviality along strata.

(2) A lemma for an admissible partition: F_i is open in X iff F̄_i is maximal for inclusion among the closed leaves.
- Open ⇒ maximal: if F_i is open and F̄_i⊊F̄_j, then F_i⊂F̄_j. Since F_i is a nonempty open set, it meets F_j, contradicting disjointness of the leaves.
- Maximal ⇒ open: if i is maximal, then for j≠i we have F̄_j∩F_i=∅. Otherwise F̄_j, being a union of leaves, would contain F_i, so F̄_i⊂F̄_j, forcing equality and hence i=j. Thus X−F_i=∪_{j≠i}F̄_j, a locally finite union of closed sets, hence closed.
The final lines restate this: F_i is open iff ∀j≠i, F̄_j⊂X−F_i, iff i is maximal. Together with the corollary on p.51 (maximality in I versus in I_U), this lets one recognise the open strata locally. It is the base step for the inductive description by a filtration X⊃X^1⊃… on p.51 (III).
errors: No mathematical error. In the closing chain ('F_i ouvert ⇔ X−F_i fermé ⇒ ∀j≠i, F̄_j⊂X−F_i ⇔ i maximal') the ⇒ is actually an equivalence, given local finiteness. The argument is slightly compressed but correct.

Condition (C) as written ('F̄_{iα}∩F_j∩U open in F_j∩U') should also require closedness, which is automatic since it is a closure intersected with F_j∩U; it then forces F̄_{iα}∩F_j∩U to be a union of components. Grothendieck's later variant 'ou encore de F_j' (open in F_j) is a slightly different, weaker reading. Minor.

ideas.what: Admissible partition = locally finite partition into locally closed pieces satisfying the frontier condition; extra requirements: connected leaves, manifold leaves (PL / semi-analytic), equisingularity
ideas.modern_name: stratification with frontier condition (Whitney/Thom-Mather stratification, tame/o-minimal stratification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1965), Thom (1969), Mather (1970); tame version: van den Dries, Shiota and others (o-minimal, 1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6 on tame topology and stratified spaces, in outline only

ideas.what: Connectedness of strata is not stable under restriction to open sets; replace it by the condition that components of U∩F_i again form an admissible partition for every open U (local frontier condition)
ideas.modern_name: local frontier condition / 'T̄∩S open in S', a consequence of local topological triviality and conic structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stratification theory (Mather, Thom; Goresky-MacPherson)

ideas.what: In an admissible partition, a leaf is open iff its closure is maximal
ideas.modern_name: open strata = maximal elements of the stratification poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly isolates, in purely topological terms, the restriction-stable form of the frontier condition for connected strata. This is a local axiom anticipating the definition of 'stratified spaces' as local objects (e.g. later sheaf/germ-theoretic treatments, exit-path categories needing conical strata). It is an early, unpublished witness of the tame-topology programme rather than a new result.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that in 1974 Grothendieck was already axiomatising stratified spaces locally (germs at points), in line with the later Esquisse programme and modern poset-stratified spaces (Lurie, Ayala-Francis-Tanaka). It holds no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard foundational material on stratifications (frontier condition, open strata = maximal strata, a localisable connectedness condition). The interest is historical: it gives a 1974 date and the topological, local axiomatics of Grothendieck's tame-topology project. The mathematics itself is folklore.
transcription_corrections: Implication in (C): the image reads 'F_{jβ} ∩ F̄_{iα} ≠ ∅ ⟹ F_{jβ} ⊂ F̄_{iα}', with the bar over F_{iα} in both places. It is not 'F̄_{jβ}∩F_{iα}'.
Line (b): the parenthetical is hard to read. 'contact d'espèces' is doubtful; it may be '(variétés de type L.P.M. ou S.A.P.M. ...)', with 'de type' or similar written as a superscript.

In (C), the phrase reads roughly 'la famille des composantes connexes des U∩F̄_i' (the bar is uncertain) 'est une partition admissible de U', followed by the inserted alternative 'c) ∀i, la famille des comp. connexes de U∩F_i est loc. finie et si ...'.
Lemma line: 'F_i ouvert de X, et F̄_i ⊊ F̄_j ⟹ F_i ouvert ≠∅ dans F̄_j et F̄_j rencontre F_i' (F_i dense in F̄_i). The transcription's '⊄' is better read as strict inclusion '⊊'.
Last lines: 'i.e. ∀j≠i, ∀k tel que F̄_k ⊋ F̄_j, on a k≠i ⟺ i maximal'.
